rapport_notes: Warm, friendly tone throughout; natural conversational rhythm and genuine interest in customer's situation.
process_discipline_notes: No repeated differentiators across stages; rep did not pause meaningfully after open-ended questions.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launches directly into logistics confirmation ('are we just moving some items?') without time-boxed framing or quid pro quo trade.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after probing: 'before we go any further did you have just kind of any concerns or any questions just off the top that I can just answer outside of pricing' — but only after logistics were already detailed.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer says 'No, not that I can think of it' and offers additional context ('storage is two miles,' 'move again in November'). Rep acknowledges but does not probe deeper into the two-move scenario or any underlying concerns.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep gives range and minimum: '2.5 to about 3 hours' and 'call wise I would be looking at 5:45 to Saturday 7:63' (likely 7:30). Personalizes slightly to TV dismount and wrapping, but no typical-move framing or explicit floor/walk/distance adjustment logic.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: None of the five Save Your Ass lines are hit. No commit-to-rate language, no 'estimate is a window' framing, no 'beats it pay less' explanation, no self-prep tip, no 'does that feel fair' close.

top_strength: Built strong rapport and efficiently gathered logistics details; successfully converted the call to a booking with a clear confirmation email follow-up.
coaching_note: Lead with quid pro quo framing ('six minutes for an accurate quote'), ask agenda before probing logistics, dig two layers deep into any concern (especially the November second move), and deliver the Save Your Ass messaging (estimate window, beats-it pay-less, self-prep tip) before close to anchor confidence in the quote.
